newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to decide on Iraq oil deal renewal this week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to decide on Iraq oil deal renewal this week.

text.p: The Clinton administration plans to decide later this week whether to approve the renewal of the Iraqi "oil-for-food" deal, which expires on June 7, U.S. State Department spokesman John Dinger said on Monday.
"That will come up for consideration later this week," he said at a news briefing. "We will study the issue closely and make our determination closer to the time of renewal."

U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on Monday recommended that the accord, which allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil for six months and use the money to buy food and medicine, should be renewed on the same terms.
The deal first went into effect in December.
Most members of the U.N. Security Council, which must decide on renewal of the deal, have said they would like to see the agreement approved under the current terms or even increased.
But the United States has reserved its position.
Dinger reiterated U.S. criticism of the Baghdad regime and its failure to adhere to U.N. Security Council resolutions.

"We're very disappointed with continued attempts by the regime in Baghdad to evade the procedures that are laid down in the memorandum of understanding that governs Resolution 986 (the oil-for-food deal)," he said.
He added that he was "disappointed" by recent statements from Baghdad that blamed the United States for the hardships facing the Iraqi people.
"It is very clear that there is only one party responsible for the suffering of the people of Iraq, and that is the regime of Saddam Hussein," Dinger said.
He said their situation could be improved if the regime stopped threatening regional stability and cleared the way for the U.N. sanctions, in place since 1990, to be removed.

The Iraqi government could "stop trying to constantly evade the restrictions" in the oil-for-food deal or use its resources to import food and humanitarian goods directly, instead of diverting those resources for "enhancing military capabilities or building palaces or building yachts."
